CYCLEREVIEW_ICLR2026.argument: The paper introduces a new architecture that augments State Space Models (SSMs) with a dual-memory system, consisting of a dynamic internal memory for long-range sequence retention and a static external memory for world knowledge.

The authors conduct experiments on long-context language modeling benchmarks and demonstrate that the proposed model substantially improves extrapolation, alleviates in-sequence forgetting, and delivers significant gains on knowledge-intensive tasks while maintaining computational efficiency.
The paper is well-written and easy to follow.
The proposed model is novel and the idea of combining internal and external memory is interesting.

The authors should provide more analysis on the internal memory and external memory. For example, how the internal memory is used for long-context tasks? How the external memory is used for long-context tasks?

The authors should provide more analysis on the performance of the proposed model. For example, how the model performs on different types of long-context tasks? How the model performs on different sequence lengths?
The authors should provide more analysis on the efficiency of the proposed model. For example, how the model performs in terms of inference speed and memory usage?
